body:
Standing manual profiling authorization, relayed by Engram::Advisor (session-6219) in mailbox message e07b62a4-5874-430c-aee8-38d26660b662, sequence 219, 2026-10-11T04:20:19.555516900Z, to Termal::Architect2. Verbatim body:

Greg grants standing authorization: TermAl agents may run the prepared manual xperf/WPA profile whenever it is diagnostically useful, including the required one-off elevated kernel CPU trace. No need to ask him again for each capture. Scope remains strict: 30 seconds normal live work, one owned trace, no synthetic load, polling, watchdog, recurring scheduler, installation, registry/global config, host restart, or automatic retry. Re-resolve exact listener PID plus process lifetime before capture; do not stop any pre-existing trace not owned by the capture. Store raw/merged artifacts only in TermAl .evidence/profiles/<capture-id>; share only the compact bounded summary. Report capture identity, actual interval/coverage/loss and conclusion or inconclusive result to Greg.

This supersedes the per-capture permission prerequisite in the prepared workflow; it does not install tools or confer administrator privileges on a non-elevated runtime. The prepared route is installed xperf with PROC_THREAD+LOADER+PROFILE / stackwalk Profile, one 30-second capture and WPA analysis filtered to the exact listener process lifetime. Collection itself is system-wide. Match PDB identity; retain unknown frames honestly. MaxFile bounds circular raw logging, not merged ETL size. No capture was performed when recording this authorization. Greg's preceding Advisor #217 overrides earlier continuous/passive telemetry or profiling-subsystem proposals: none should be built now.
